item.title: Principal specializations of the $t$-chromatic symmetric function
item.description: arXiv:2610.31785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the $t$-chromatic symmetric function $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, a variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function in which the variable $t$ records the number of distinct colors used in a proper coloring. Although $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$ is equivalent to the chromatic symmetric function as a graph invariant, its principal specializations retain substantially more information than those of the chromatic symmetric function. This construction is motivated by the work of Bajo--Beck--Vindas-Mel\'endez on the $q$-chromatic polynomial and the conjecture of Loehr--Warrington that the $n$th principal specialization of the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees on at most $n$ vertices, both of which stem from Stanley's longstanding question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees. We determine the classes of caterpillars resulting from the second principal specialization of $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, showing that the second specialization already captures some of the structure of trees. We then prove that the third principal specialization distinguishes and explicitly reconstructs caterpillars with three spine vertices as well as elongated bistars. Finally, we conjecture, based on computational data, that the fourth principal specialization distinguishes all caterpillars.
item.dc:creator: Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, Mary Claire Simone

item.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
item.description: arXiv:2610.31795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.
item.dc:creator: Sara Billey, Herman Chau, Kevin Liu

item.title: Additive energy and Fourier complexity of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the additive energy and the Fourier approximation of graph adjacency matrices labeled by a cyclic group. For a graph with $N$ vertices, $s$ edges and adjacency matrix $M$, the additive energy of its directed edge set is at most $\min\{(2s)^3,N^2\operatorname{tr}(M^4)\}$, and equality in the spectral bound holds exactly when the labeling attains the graph-energy lower bound for the Fourier ratio. Such a labeling also minimizes every best $k$-term Fourier approximation error, whose square equals the tail of the squared adjacency singular values. We prove that graphs of odd prime-power order admit an equality-attaining labeling exactly when they are cyclic Cayley graphs, and a connected example on $15$ vertices shows that equality need not imply vertex transitivity at other orders. We construct regular graph families with asymptotically maximal normalized additive edge energy and unbounded minimum Fourier ratio, one of them with density tending to one half. For dense graph sequences under uniformly random labelings, the collision dimension differs from the reciprocal squared edge density by a quantity tending to zero in probability. We also prove a quantitative stability estimate for the graph-energy bound and show why its dependence on a spectral scale cannot be omitted, even for regular graphs. For a rank-$m$ orthogonal projector we prove $m\leq D_4\leq\operatorname{FR}^2$, characterize the equality $D_4=m$ by cyclic translation invariance, and obtain a quantitative approximation by a circulant projector.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Gupta, Sam Ferguson, Alex Iosevich, Joshua Iosevich, Haoyuan Tian, Ben Song

item.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.
item.dc:creator: Hac\`{e}ne Belbachir, Jos\'{e} Ricardo G. Mendon\c{c}a

item.title: Swapping Compatible Words
item.description: arXiv:2610.31967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality iff $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. In 2024 Carrigan et. al. asked if there is a "natural" bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a "natural" bijection $\Phi$ from the set of all finite words to itself such that a word $\Omega$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $\Phi(\Omega)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $\Omega$ into $\Phi(\Omega)$.
item.dc:creator: Ramin Naimi

item.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy. The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Muchen Ju, Junjie Ni, Kaixin Wang, Yihan Xiao

item.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.
item.dc:creator: Seonbin Kim

item.title: Equifacetted polytopes whose facets are products of simplices: The simplicial prism case
item.description: arXiv:2610.32035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study \emph{prismatical} polytopes, those all of whose facets are combinatorially isomorphic to the simplicial prism $\Delta^{d-2}\times\Delta^1$. In dimension three these are exactly the cubical polytopes, so the class sits naturally between simplicial and cubical polytopes. In dimension four, $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$ is the simplest prismatical polytope and we can construct infinitely many by using connected sums. By fibreing a triangle over a triangulated polygon we construct infinitely many connected-sum-prime prismatical $4$-polytopes. Finally, we show that there are no prismatical $d$-polytopes for $d\ge5$, answering a question of Perles and Shephard.
item.dc:creator: Federico Castillo, Guillermo Pi\~neda-Villavicencio, Jos\'e Alejandro Samper

item.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.32050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxuan Chen, Chance Crigler, Shengtao Ding, Dana Paquin, Julian Schennach

item.title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colon\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^\alpha$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{\alpha+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]
item.dc:creator: Matija Blagojevi\'c, Pavle V. M. Blagojevi\'c

item.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.32192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid $3.12.12$, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid $4.8.8$, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid $3.6.3.6$, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid $4.6.12$, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid $3.4.6.4$, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.
item.dc:creator: Rudini Sampaio

item.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.
item.dc:creator: Yansong Feng, Hao Jiang, Guancheng Li, Tianyi Li, Lili Tang

item.title: Saturation in three-uniform Berge hypergraphs: the five-star spectrum and the $K_4$ saturation number
item.description: arXiv:2610.32353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph \(G\), a hypergraph is Berge-\(G\)-saturated if it contains no Berge copy of \(G\), but adding any missing hyperedge creates one. We determine the complete saturation spectrum of three-uniform Berge five-stars for every order. For \(n\ge7\), every integer from \(\lceil4n/3\rceil-3\) to \(2n-5\) occurs; the additional values depend only on \(n\) modulo five. The structural ingredient is a sharp bound on the remainder after deleting all complete five-vertex components: for an \(n\)-vertex, \(m\)-edge Berge-five-star-saturated hypergraph, this remainder has at most \(15(2n-m)/7\) vertices. We characterize all equality cases. We also prove that every three-uniform Berge-\(K_4\)-saturated hypergraph on \(n\ge7\) vertices has at least \(n\) edges. Together with known constructions, this determines its saturation number for every order and settles the conjecture of Chen, He, and Xie; the new lower bound covers the previously unresolved orders \(9\le n\le95\). Both arguments use the distinct representatives forced by saturation to obtain local incidence constraints. For five-stars these constraints bound the size of the remainder and characterize equality. For \(K_4\), they reduce a putative counterexample to a configuration on at most eight vertices; incidence estimates and a sharp bound on the vertices covered by short cycles in a bipartite graph exclude all remaining cases.
item.dc:creator: XuanYu Cao, Yuan Lai, Chunxiang Wang

item.title: The chromatic number of $\{\mathrm{ISK}_4, \textup{diamond}\}$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. L\'ev\^eque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs. We prove this conjecture for diamond-free graphs. Moreover, the bound is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Qing Cui, Kaiyang Lan

item.title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.32408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $\chi (S^n_{R}) \leq (\xi_R + o(1))^n$, where $\xi_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-1/(4R^2)) $ and $\chi(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.
item.dc:creator: A. I. Bikeev, V. A. Voronov, A. M. Raigorodskii

item.title: An incidence approach to cross-intersection in semilattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an incidence-based method for product bounds on cross-intersecting families in finite graded meet-semilattices. The two families may lie in different rank or type fibres and may have different design strengths. The criterion separates global incidence parameters from two directional local counts and yields the sharp product bound, with equality only for full stars with a common centre. Applications include mixed subspace types relative to a fixed subspace, a type-restricted generator family in $Q^-(7,q)$, and mixed form ranks in symplectic spaces. The same short criterion gives several sharp results not obtained directly from the specific theorems and general criteria compared here. In the singular-space case, it also applies in an infinite parameter range beyond the natural star-ratio and weak-spreadness tests.
item.dc:creator: Sho Suda

item.title: The upper bounds on occupancy fraction and variance fraction for linear regular uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hard-core model can be used to understand the number of independent sets in graphs in extremal graph theory. The occupancy and variance fractions are the expectation and variance, respectively, of the independent-set size, normalized by the number of vertices. We provide upper bounds on the occupancy and variance fractions of linear $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraphs for small positive fugacities. In proving these results, we use the cluster expansion and the abstract polymer models, two tools from statistical physics, to analyse auxiliary functions associated with independence polynomials, comparing their low-order coefficients and controlling the remainders uniformly in the number of vertices.
item.dc:creator: Weiyuan Zhang, Kexiang Xu

item.title: New approaches to the Erd\H{o}s Distinct Subset Sums Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.32580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new method of reproving the best known lower bound of the Erd\H{o}s distinct subset sums problem. Although our lower bound is asymptotically the same as in Dubroff, Fox and Xu, it is slightly better for the case when \(n\) is odd. Besides, we also provide a new lower bound on the second largest element \(a_{n-1}\).
item.dc:creator: Aren Hasratyan, Mikl\'os Ruszink\'o

item.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of 3-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"{e}te, and Yu that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the "depth-$t$ iterated blowup" $\textsf{B}_t$ for an integer $t\geq 0$. Here, the $3$-graphs $\textsf{B}_t$ are defined recursively: $\textsf{B}_0$ has one vertex, and $\textsf{B}_t$ for $t\geq 1$ is obtained from the disjoint union of three copies of $\textsf{B}_{t-1}$ by adding all transversal hyperedges.
item.dc:creator: Lior Gishboliner, Sepehr Hajebi, Xiangyu Li

item.title: Sharp asymmetric vertex-Ramsey properties of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1992, \L uczak, Ruci\'{n}ski and Voigt showed that for any graph $H$, a parameter $m_1(H)$ - called the 1-density - governs the threshold at which the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ inherits the vertex-Ramsey property. In 2000, Friedgut and Krivelevich showed this threshold is sharp for graphs satisfying a natural balancedness condition. In 1996, Kreuter showed that for any graphs $H_1, \ldots, H_r$ with $m_1(H_1) \geq \cdots \geq m_1(H_r)$, a parameter dependent only on $H_1$ and $H_2$ governs the threshold at which $G(n,p)$ inherits the `asymmetric' vertex-Ramsey property. We prove this threshold is sharp for graphs respecting natural balancedness conditions, including in the analogous hypergraph setting.
item.dc:creator: Robert Hancock, Joseph Hyde, Mael Kupperschmitt

item.title: Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six
item.description: arXiv:2610.32717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings. In a minimum counterexample, two local boundary colorings force the degree-four vertices to have disjoint neighborhoods. A characterization of the local extension obstructions permits these vertices to be restored simultaneously. The proof uses Hamiltonian-connectedness of four-connected planar graphs and the computer-assisted Four-Color Theorem; it requires no further computation.
item.dc:creator: Enqiang Zhu

item.title: A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $\delta\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-\delta+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $\delta$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$. Such a subspace is maximum $h$-scattered if and only if the kernel of $A$ contains no nonzero vector whose expansion with respect to an $\mathbb{F}_q$-basis of $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ has rank weight at most $h+1$. When $\gcd(n,s)=1$, $R$ is a field, and a first-moment argument, counting these vectors up to multiplication by $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*\mathbb{F}_{q^s}^*$, shows that with positive probability the kernel contains none of them if $s>h(n-h-2)$. When $d=\gcd(n,s)>1$, $R$ is a product of $d$ fields, and vectors vanishing in some factors lie in the kernel with larger probability. We control them by proving that, for an $(h+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $D$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, the elements of $D\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ vanishing outside $k$ given factors, $0<k<d$, form an $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-space of dimension at most $(h+1)k/d$, with equality only if $D$ is linear over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ larger than $\mathbb{F}_q$. Taking $s=gr/(h+1)$ gives the bound on $r$. Finally, if $(n-h-1)\mid(h+1)$, then for every $r$ satisfying the above inequality there is an $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ of dimension $\lfloor rn/(h+1)\rfloor$, without a divisibility condition on $rn$.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Giannoni, Alessandro Neri

item.title: Triangle-Free Sets in Exact-Distance Hamming Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T_q(n,r)$ be the largest size of a vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph of the graph on $[q]^n$ whose edges join words at Hamming distance $r$. We study this quantity for fixed alphabet size and fixed distance, with particular emphasis on the ternary cube. Alphabet restriction transfers the binary fixed-distance theorem of Balogh, Chen, and Li to give $T_q(n,2h)=O_h(q^n/n^h)$. We extend the known distance-one formula and distance-two order to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, obtaining $T_q(n,1)=2q^{n-1}$ and $T_q(n,2)=\Theta_q(q^n/n)$, and establish $T_3(n,4)=\Theta(3^n/n^2)$. For general fixed distance, we prove \[ T_q(n,r)=\Omega_{q,r}\!\left( \frac{q^n\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{(r+\lfloor r/2\rfloor)/2}} \right)\qquad(q\ge3), \] while we show that $T_q(n,r)=\Omega_{q,r}(q^n/n^{\lfloor(q-1)r/q\rfloor})$ holds for prime-power $q$ and $r\ge2$ via the extended BCH parity-check constructions. At distance three, we construct coordinate weights avoiding bounded-coefficient three-term relations and obtain \[ T_q(n,3)\ge q^n/[n\exp(O_q(\sqrt{\log n}))]. \] Our main ternary construction combines cap partitions, multicolor triangle Ramsey colorings, and a quadratic map to obtain \[ T_3(n,3)=\Omega\!\left( \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\,3^n\right). \] A coordinate-line counting argument gives the complementary upper bound $T_3(n,3)\le(5/27+O(n^{-1}))3^n$, together with an explicit bound for every fixed $q\ge3$. Whether the ternary density tends to zero remains open.
item.dc:creator: Bence Csajb\'ok, Padmini Mukkamala, Zolt\'an L\'or\'ant Nagy

item.title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
item.description: arXiv:2610.32798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by H\"orsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of H\"orsch et al.
item.dc:creator: Siyue Liu, Taihei Oki, Chao Xu

item.title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.
item.dc:creator: Maximus Lu

item.title: The Tur\'an number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Gy\H{o}ri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path. We consider the setting in which the host hypergraph is connected. Let $\operatorname{ex}^{\mathrm{conn}}_r(n,\mathcal{BP}_k)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex, $r$-uniform, connected hypergraph that does not contain a Berge path on $k$ vertices. This number was determined by Zhang, Broersma, Gy\H{o}ri, Tompkins, Wang for $k \leq r+2$, and Zhao, Gerbner, Zhou for $k \geq 2r+2$. In this paper, we resolved the remaining cases $r+3 \leq k \leq 2r+1$ when $n$ is sufficiently large, confirming a conjecture of Zhang, et al.
item.dc:creator: Yupei Li, Ruth Luo

item.title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index
item.description: arXiv:2610.32897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices. It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight. In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Alexander Vlasov, Svetlana Zhilina

item.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
item.description:
arXiv:2610.31556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor rac{d-1}{2}floor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$. The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $
u=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $
u\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $
u\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $
u\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Anghel, Rares Stan

item.title: Links of minimum degree and exact covering numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The covering number $C(v,k,t)$ is the least number of $k$-subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset lies in one of them. We reduce the question whether a covering with $L$ blocks exists to the classification of links. If every point of such a covering lies in at least $r$ blocks and $(r+1)v>kL$, some point lies in exactly $r$ blocks, and its link, the blocks through it with the point removed, is a $(v-1,k-1,t-1)$-covering with $r$ blocks. It then suffices to list these links up to isomorphism, to prove the list complete, and to show that no link in the list extends to a covering with $L$ blocks. Completeness is certified by one unsatisfiable formula that excludes the listed classes, so the program that lists the links need not be trusted. In general the last two steps are decided by propositional satisfiability (SAT) solving, with every formula written by two separately implemented encoders and every refutation checked by a formally verified proof checker. For links with four blocks and $t=3$ we give the classification by hand, under a condition on the parameters. As an application we determine twenty-five covering numbers with $t\in\{3,4,5\}$ in which the published lower bound was one less than the size of a known covering, among them $C(39,24,3)=9$.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Gippini Requeijo

item.title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.31837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms. Their presheaf structure yields a deletion-contraction homotopy pushout, from which we derive a uniform combinatorial proof of the integral cohomology presentation for all $n \geq 2$. This presentation is natural with respect to weak maps and identifies cohomology rings with higher Orlik-Solomon algebras extending the known formulas for linear arrangements to non-realizable oriented matroids. Finally, we equip Deligne groupoids with a presheaf structure and identify them functorially with the fundamental groupoids of the complexified complements.
item.dc:creator: Basile Coron, Denis Lyskov

item.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.32056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.
item.dc:creator: Nardo Gim\'enez, Juan Francisco Gottig, Miguel Palacios, Mariana P\'erez, Melina Privitelli

item.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons
item.description: arXiv:2610.32147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a neural exploratory framework for variational problems over graphons, i.e., symmetric measurable functions $[0,1]^2 \to [0,1]$, that arise as limits of dense graph sequences. Such problems are central to two parts of the mathematical literature: extremal graph theory, which studies graph parameter optimisation under given restrictions, often for those graphs with a large number of vertices, and the large deviation theory of dense random graphs, which characterises the structure of rare events through constrained graphon optimisation. We represent graphons by implicit neural networks and optimise graphon objectives by gradient descent. Our design combines three ingredients: a multi-scale sinusoidal residual architecture biased toward sharp, step-like graphons; an embedded solver that enforces a single empirical density constraint and is differentiated by implicit differentiation; and symmetry-aware Monte Carlo estimators. On generalised Tur\'an problems that previously required substantial human effort, our framework rediscovers known optimal graphons without human intervention. Applied to open instances, it produces candidate optima, including a previously unreported family of extremal structures. Applied to the variational problems from the large deviation theory of Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs, the framework produces new candidate optimal graphons across both upper- and lower-tail regimes for multiple pattern graphs; for the case of the triangle graph and the upper-tail regime, these candidates improve upon the best-known reference construction of Lubetzky and Zhao. The structures found by our framework have also led to new theorems on the optimal graphons for both families of problems.
item.dc:creator: Taeyoung Kim, Jineon Baek, Joonkyung Lee, Hongseok Yang

item.title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.32219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erd\H{o}s--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Lin Chen, Tingwei Hu, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang

item.title: Cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A graph is edge-transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its edge set. This paper is devoted to a systematic study of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$, where $p$ is a prime and $\ell$ is an even integer. We first show that either $\Gamma$ is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph of order $18$, or its full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(\Gamma)$ contains a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ which is isomorphic to either $Z_{p^2}$ or $Z_{p}^2$. For the case $P\cong Z_{p^2}$, we prove that $\Gamma$ is either arc-regular or edge-regular, and provide a complete classification of such graphs. For the case $P\cong Z_{p}^2$, we prove that $\Gamma$ is a normal cover of certain known graphs. This work generalizes previous classifications by Zhou and Feng (2024), Lu et al.~(2004), and others. As an application, we obtain a classification of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$ in the case where $\ell$ is square-free.
item.dc:creator: Xue Wang, Jun-Jie Huang, Da-Wei Yang

item.title: Stable Set Reconfiguration in Dense Digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a directed graph, a stable (or acyclic) set is a set which does not induce a directed cycle. Given a directed graph and two acyclic sets of the same size, the Acyclic-Set-Reconfiguration with Directed Token Sliding (ASR) problem asks whether one can, by iteratively replacing a vertex by an adjacent one, transform the first set into the second one, while maintaining acyclicity during the transformation. In this work, we present a study of the complexity of ASR and provide an FPT algorithm for semi-complete digraphs, when parametrized by the size of the sets being reconfigured, the directed pathwidth (or equivalently, the directed treewidth) of the instance, and a newly introduced parameter called the iteration of the reconfiguration sequence. To the best of our knowledge, the reconfiguration of stable sets has only been studied on undirected graphs, or (more recently) on sparse directed graphs.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Houdaigoui, Nacim Oijid, Matthieu Petiteau, Alexandre Vigny

item.title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank. In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: The totally nonnegative wonderful compactification of G is a ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.32745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\overline{G}$ denote the wonderful compactification of a semisimple algebraic group $G$ of adjoint type. We use contractive flows to show that the totally nonnegative part of every $G \times G$ orbit closure of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In particular, the totally nonnegative part of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed ball.
item.dc:creator: Sam Evens, Steven N. Karp

item.title: The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements
item.description: arXiv:2610.32761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive. When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral. An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering. We show that the reduced decompositions of a cameral Coxeter elements for which the underlying set S satisfies that (W, S ) is a Coxeter system, are necessarily cameral, and we count the number of chambers from which a cameral Coxeter element can be obtained. We show that one can go through all these chambers using the restricted Hurwitz action on the set of cameral decompositions, which is generated by transpositions of adjacent commuting reflections and by the Garside element {\delta} of the dual Garside structure, which acts by a quiver mutation of the orientation of the Coxeter diagram.
item.dc:creator: Emir Melliti

item.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.
item.dc:creator: Haoming Wang, Ming Yuan

item.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
item.description: arXiv:2610.32832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur. In the latter case, $h>1$. This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.
item.dc:creator: Gaston Burrull, Zhitong Alex Li, Shixuan Zeng

item.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $\eta\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\le\eta\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons. In this work we solve this variational problem for every $\eta\in(0,1)$. We show that every minimizer is either a constant graphon or a step graphon with two blocks of equal size. Correspondingly, the conditioned graph is close to an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph or to a symmetric stochastic block model with two blocks. These two regimes are separated by a first order phase transition at the threshold $\eta_*=0.009217\ldots$. This resolves a conjecture of Zhao [78] and an open problem of Janson and Warnke [39] on triangles. It thereby gives a complete description of the lower tail of triangle counts in this range of $p$.
item.dc:creator: Dong Huang, Shuangping Li

item.title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
item.description: arXiv:2610.32954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. We investigate the complexity of two such problems, whose directed counterparts are well-known. Our first result is an $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for the alternating $k$-linkage problem on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. This problem asks for $k$ vertex-disjoint alternating paths joining $k$ prescribed pairs of vertices. This generalizes the directed $k$-linkage algorithm for DAGs. For every fixed $k$, this also yields a polynomial-time algorithm for finding $k$ internally vertex-disjoint alternating $(s,t)$-paths, solving an open problem by Abouelaoualim et al. from 2008. We then consider the alternating chromatic number of $2$-edge-coloured graphs, defined as the minimum number of parts in a vertex partition such that each part induces an acyclic subgraph. This notion is analogous to the dichromatic number of digraphs, where it is known that deciding dichromatic number $2$ is NP-complete even on tournaments. Our second result is that deciding alternating chromatic number $2$ is NP-complete on complete $2$-edge-coloured graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether a graph can be partitioned into two induced threshold graphs is NP-complete.
item.dc:creator: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, St\'ephane Bessy, Amadeus Reinald

item.title: The evolution of random subgraphs of the permutahedron
item.description: arXiv:2404.17260v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In their seminal paper introducing the theory of random graphs, Erd\H{o}s and R\'{e}nyi considered the evolution of the structure of a random subgraph of $K_n$ as the density increases from $0$ to $1$, identifying two key points in this evolution -- the percolation threshold, where the order of the largest component seemingly jumps from logarithmic to linear in size, and the connectivity threshold, where the subgraph becomes connected. Similar phenomena have been observed in many other random graph models, and in particular, works of Ajtai, Koml\'{o}s and Szemer\'{e}di and of Erd\H{o}s and Spencer determine corresponding thresholds for random subgraphs of the hypercube. The permutahedron, like the hypercube, has many equivalent representations, and arises as a natural object of study in many areas of combinatorics. In particular, as a highly-symmetric simple polytope, like the $n$-simplex and $n$-cube, percolation on the permutahedron arises naturally as an analogue to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi random graph and the percolated hypercube. We determine the percolation threshold and the connectivity threshold for random subgraphs of the permutahedron. Along the way we develop a novel graph exploration technique which can be used to find exponentially large clusters after percolation in high-dimensional geometric graphs, and we initiate the study of the isoperimetric properties of the permutahedron.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Collares, Joseph Doolittle, Joshua Erde

item.title: Chromatic Ramsey numbers and two-color Tur\'an densities
item.description: arXiv:2409.07535v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a graph $G$, its $2$-color Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph, such that the edges can be colored with two colors avoiding a monochromatic copy of $G$. Let $\pi^{(2)}(G)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)/\binom{n}{2}$ be the $2$-color Tur\'{a}n density of $G$. What real numbers in the interval $(0,1)$ are realized as the $2$-color Tur\'{a}n density of some graph? It is known that $\pi^{(2)}(G)=1-(R_{\chi}(G)-1)^{-1}$, where $R_{\chi}(G)$ is the chromatic Ramsey number of $G$. Burr, Erd\H{o}s, and Lov\'{a}sz showed that $(k-1)^2+1\leq{R_{\chi}(G)}\leq{R(k)}$, for any $k$-chromatic graph $G$, where $R(k)$ is the classical Ramsey number. However, it is an open problem to determine how many distinct values between $(k-1)^{2}+1$ and $R(k)$ can be realized as $R_{\chi}(G)$ of some $k$-chromatic graph $G$ for general $k$. In this paper, among others, we prove that there are $\Omega(k)$ different values of $R_{\chi}(G)$ among $k$-chromatic graphs $G$. This sheds more light onto the possible $2$-color Tur\'{a}n densities of graphs.
item.dc:creator: Maria Axenovich, Simon Gaa, Dingyuan Liu

item.title: Subset selection problems in planar point sets
item.description: arXiv:2412.14287v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a finite point set satisfying condition $\mathcal{A}$, the subset selection problem asks, how large of a subset satisfying condition $\mathcal{B}$ can be extracted? In this paper, we make progress on three instances of subset selection problems in planar point sets. Let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq s$, and let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points, where at most $s$ points lie on the same line. Firstly, we select a general position subset of $P$. This problem was proposed by Erd\H{o}s under the regime when $s$ is a constant. For $s$ being non-constant, we give new lower and upper bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, we show that in the worst case such a set can have size at most $O(n^{5/6+o(1)}/\sqrt{s})$ when $3\leq s\leq n^{1/3}$ and $O(n/s)$ when $n^{1/3}\leq s\leq n$. Secondly, we select a monotone general position subset of $P$, that is, a subset in general position where the points are ordered from left to right and their $y$-coordinates are either non-decreasing or non-increasing. We present bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, when $s=\Omega(\sqrt{n})$, our upper and lower bounds differ at most by a logarithmic factor. Lastly, we select a subset of $P$ with pairwise distinct slopes. This problem was initially studied by Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Ruzsa, and Taylor on the grid. We show that for $s=O(\sqrt{n})$ such a subset of size $\Omega((n/\log{s})^{1/3})$ can always be found in $P$. When $s=\Theta(\sqrt{n})$, this matches a lower bound given by Zhang on the grid. As for the upper bound, we show that in the worst case such a subset has size at most $O(\sqrt{n})$ for $2\leq s\leq n^{3/8}$ and $O((n/s)^{4/5})$ for $n^{3/8}\leq s=O(\sqrt{n})$. The proofs use a wide range of tools such as incidence geometry, probabilistic methods, the hypergraph container method, and additive combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: J\'ozsef Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen, Adrian Dumitrescu, Dingyuan Liu

item.title: The number of regular simplices in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2507.19841v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the extremal function $S^k_d(n)$, defined as the maximum number of regular $(k-1)$-simplices spanned by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For any fixed $d\geq2k\geq6$, we determine the asymptotic behavior of $S^k_d(n)$ up to a lower-order term. In particular, when $k=3$, we determine the exact value of $S^3_d(n)$, for all even dimensions $d\geq6$ and sufficiently large $n$. This resolves a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. The proof leverages techniques from hypergraph Tur\'an theory and linear algebra.
item.dc:creator: Felix Christian Clemen, Adrian Dumitrescu, Dingyuan Liu

item.title: Palindromic switching rook polynomials and domino-stable collections of cells
item.description: arXiv:2511.13982v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a finite collection of cells. Two non-attacking rook configurations on $\mathcal{P}$ are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of switches inside rectangles contained in $\mathcal{P}$. The switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ enumerates the resulting equivalence classes according to the number of rooks. We characterize the collections of cells whose switching rook polynomial is palindromic. More precisely, we introduce a new combinatorial property, called domino-stability, and we prove that the switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ is palindromic if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Giancarlo Rinaldo

item.title: Counterexamples to a dimension-free variant of Erd\H{o}s's diameter conjecture for separated distances
item.description: arXiv:2604.15305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Erd\H{o}s asked about the least possible diameter of an $n$-point set in Euclidean space when any two pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. We consider the uniform-in-dimension variant of his question, in which the dimension $d$ may grow with $n$ and the error term is independent of $d$, and answer it in the negative by an explicit construction. For every prime power $q$, we construct a set $\mathcal X_n$ of $n=q+1$ points in $\mathbb R^{q^2+q}=\mathbb R^{n^2-n}$ such that the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances are mutually at least $1$ apart, yet $$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X_n)\le \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\Bigr)n^2.$$ The construction combines a Singer cyclic difference set with a weighted product of $N=\binom n2$ regular $m$-gons, where $m=q^2+q+1$. The weights are chosen so that the resulting distances increase while the gaps between consecutive distances decrease. After normalizing the smallest gap to $1$, all distinct pairwise distances are separated by at least $1$, while the diameter has asymptotic constant $1-1/\pi^2<1$.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: Spanning Subdivisions in Robustly Expanding Digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.27452v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: K\"uhn, Osthus and Treglown [\emph{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} \textbf{100} (2010)] proved that every sufficiently large robust outexpander with linear minimum semi-degree contains a Hamilton cycle. In this paper, we extend their result to spanning subdivisions of a digraph $F$ in a robust outexpander $D$, with prescribed branch vertices and arbitrarily specified path lengths. In particular, the digraph $F$ need not be fixed. For an $n$-vertex digraph $D$, $F$ may have as many as a constant multiple of $n/\log n$ arcs. This holds provided that $F$ has sufficiently few vertices and the prescribed lengths satisfy suitable conditions. We further establish a more general result for mixed prescribed path lengths, which allows $F$ to have linearly many arcs when the shorter replacement paths together use only a small proportion of the vertices of $D$. As applications, we obtain spanning subdivision extensions of the asymptotic Nash--Williams theorem for digraphs and an asymptotically sharp Ore-type theorem for oriented graphs.
item.dc:creator: Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei, Jin Yan

item.title: Amply regular graphs with $\mu$ close to half the valency and group divisible designs
item.description: arXiv:2605.25754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we classify connected amply regular graphs with diameter $d \geq 4$ and parameters $(v, k, \lambda, \mu)$ satisfying $\mu = \frac{k-1}{2}$, where $k\geq 5$ is odd. We prove that such a graph must be exactly one of the following: the $5$-cube, the graph $\K_2 \square \Lambda$, where $\Lambda$ is the unique bipartite $(0,2)$-graph on $14$ vertices, or the point--block incidence graph of a group divisible design with the dual property, namely a $GDDDP\left(2, k+1;\, k;\, 0, \frac{k-1}{2}\right)$. For the last family, we give equivalent characterizations in terms of bipartite $Q$-regular graphs and relation graphs of symmetric association schemes with five classes. Furthermore, we present constructions of such amply regular graphs, yielding infinite families of examples derived from Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and Paley digraphs.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jin, Jack H. Koolen, Chenhui Lv

item.title: The Size of the Intersection of $q$-ary Hamming Balls
item.description: arXiv:2606.09158v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interest in studying the size of the intersection of multiple $q$-ary Hamming balls has grown due to the recent advances in DNA-based data storage systems. We present an exact formula for the cardinality of the intersection of $s$ Hamming balls of varying radii over a $q$-ary alphabet. It is known that the distances between the center points of the Hamming balls are not enough, in general, to determine the size of the intersection. Based on our formula, we are able to find more refined structural properties of the center points for determining the exact size of the intersection. Moreover, we also analyze the size of the intersection of Hamming balls with equal radii $t$ for sufficiently large $n$ when $t$ and $q$ are constants. When $s=3$, we give the necessary and sufficient conditions (for all $q\ge 2$, $q\neq 6$ and sufficiently large $n$) to obtain the maximum size of the intersection when the centers of the Hamming balls have a given minimum distance and demonstrate how to compute it using our general formula.
item.dc:creator: Ville Junnila, Tero Laihonen, Tuomo Lehtil\"a, Pavan Padavu Devaraj

item.title: Near-optimal Tur\'an densities of $r$-graphs on $r+1$ vertices
item.description: arXiv:2608.18924v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\pi(H)$ be the Tur\'an density of an r-uniform hypergraph $H$ and let $H_k^r$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph on $r+1$ vertices with exactly $k$ edges, where $1\le k\le r+1$. Sidorenko~(JCT-B, 2024) proved that $\pi(H_3^r)\ge (1.7215-o(1))r^{-2}$ as $r\to\infty$ and $\pi(H_k^r)\ge (C_k+o(1))r^{-(1+1/(k-2))}$ for fixed $k$ as $r\to\infty$. Clemen~later improved the first bound to $\pi(H_3^r)\ge cr^{-2}\sqrt{\log r}$ for some constant $c>0$. In this article, we prove the following results. \begin{itemize} \item For any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c_\varepsilon>0$ such that $$\pi(H_3^r)\ge \frac{c_\varepsilon}{r(\log r)^{2+\varepsilon}}.$$ %$\pi(H_3^r)\ge 1/(r(\log r)^{2+o(1)})$. Together with the known upper bound $\pi(H_3^r)\le1/r$, this implies $\pi(H_3^r)=r^{-1+o(1)}$. \item For every $3\le k\le r+1$, let $s=\min\{k-2,r-k+2\}$. Then \begin{equation*} 0\le \frac{k-2}{r}-\pi(H_k^r) \le \frac{128}{r}\left(\sqrt{s\log\frac{er}{s}}+\log\frac{er}{s}\right). \end{equation*} This estimate yields several asymptotically sharp results for $\pi(H_k^r)$. For example, $\pi(H_k^r)=(1+o(1))(k-2)/r$ when $\log(er/(k))=o(k)$. \end{itemize}
item.dc:creator: Jiabao Yang, Xiutao Zhu

item.title: Broadcast Domination Number is at Most Twice the Multipacking Number
item.description: arXiv:2608.20036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a graph $ G = (V, E) $ with a vertex set $ V $ and an edge set $ E $, a function $ f : V \rightarrow \{0, 1, 2, . . . , diam(G)\} $ is called a \emph{broadcast} on $ G $. For each vertex $ u \in V $, if there exists a vertex $ v $ in $ G $ (possibly, $ u = v $) such that $ f (v) > 0 $ and $ d(u, v) \leq f (v) $, then $ f $ is called a dominating broadcast on $ G $. The cost of the dominating broadcast $f$ is the quantity $ \sum_{v\in V}f(v) $. The minimum cost of a dominating broadcast is the broadcast domination number of $G$, denoted by $ \gamma_{b}(G) $. A multipacking is a set $ M \subseteq V $ in a graph $ G = (V, E) $ such that for every vertex $ v \in V $ and for every integer $ r \geq 1 $, the ball of radius $ r $ around $ v $ contains at most $ r $ vertices of $ M $, that is, there are at most $ r $ vertices in $ M $ at a distance at most $ r $ from $ v $ in $ G $. The multipacking number of $ G $ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking of $ G $ and is denoted by $ mp(G) $. It is known that $mp(G)\leq\gamma_b(G)$. In 2014, Hartnell and Mynhardt proved that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 3mp(G)-2$ whenever $mp(G)\geq2$. In 2019, Beaudou, Brewster, and Foucaud improved this bound to $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)+3$ and conjectured that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$. We solve their conjecture by proving that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$ for every graph $G$. Our proof is constructive and yields a linear-time $2$-approximation algorithm for Maximum Multipacking problem which improves the earlier approximation factor $2+o(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Sk Samim Islam

item.title: A Method of Construction of Pairwise Additive Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
item.description: arXiv:2608.21048v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The existence of sets of balanced incomplete block (BIB) designs with pairwise additivity, called pairwise additive BIB designs, has been studied through direct and recursive constructions in the literature. This paper presents a new method of constructing such designs from affine resolvable semi-regular group divisible (ARSRGD) designs. Since many known ARSRGD designs are obtained from generalized Hadamard matrices, we also describe the corresponding construction of pairwise additive BIB designs from generalized Hadamard matrices. Using the construction together with known existence results for generalized Hadamard matrices, we obtain several new infinite series of pairwise additive BIB designs, including designs with parameter sets whose existence was previously unknown.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Matsubara, Satoru Kadowaki

item.title: Extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles
item.description: arXiv:2608.22414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an integer $k\geq2$ and a graph $F$, the $k$-uniform suspension $\mathcal{S}^kF$ is obtained by adjoining a fixed set of $k-2$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. In this paper, we study two extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles. Write $K^k_t$ for the $k$-uniform clique of order $t$. Let $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ and $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^k_t,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ denote the maximum numbers of edges and copies of $K^k_t$, respectively, in an $\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell}$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every $k\geq2$ and infinitely many $n$, \[\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)=\frac{n^{k-1/2}}{(k+1)!}+O(n^{k-1}).\] This extends a folklore result for $k=2$ and, as an immediate consequence, yields the asymptotics of $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ for infinitely many $n$, previously established by Mubayi (for all $n$). Furthermore, for every $k\geq2$ and $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we determine the order of magnitude \[\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})=\Theta(n^{k-1+1/\ell}).\] This generalizes both the classical graph case $k=2$ and a previous result of Mukherjee for $k=\ell=3$. The principal difficulty in both problems lies in constructing the lower bounds. Our construction for $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ incorporates a novel block-packing structure, which yields substantially more copies of $K^k_{k+1}$ than previously known constructions. For $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ with $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we establish a natural $k$-uniform version of Wenger graphs, addressing the subtleties involved in lifting extremal graph constructions to suspensions. We also give applications of our results to Tur\'an problems for simplicial complexes.
item.dc:creator: Dingyuan Liu

item.title: A Topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman Theorem and its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2609.10402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a topological generalization of the Figiel--Lindenstrauss--Milman inequality, answering a recent question of Frick, Hosseini, and Vasileuski: every nonempty strongly regular CW complex with $v$ vertices, $f$ maximal cells, and a free involution that permutes its cells has $\mathbb Z/2$-index at most $4\log v\log f$. The classical inequality for centrally symmetric polytopes is the special case of polytope boundaries. As an application, we show that every finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb RP^d$ has at least $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt d))$ vertices. The previous best lower bound was $\Omega(d^2)$. We also construct triangulations with $\exp(O(\sqrt d))$ vertices. Using the same method, we prove a low-dimensional Postnikov factorization theorem, which gives similar vertex lower bounds for several classical families, such as complex and quaternionic projective spaces, the $d$-torus, closed symplectic and aspherical manifolds, Grassmannians, classical Lie groups, and spherical space forms. Further applications include results in learning theory, convex geometry, computational topology, and topological bounds for chromatic numbers and Vietoris--Rips complexes.
item.dc:creator: Florian Frick, Kaave Hosseini, Eric Myzelev, Arya Narnapatti, Aliaksei Vasileuski

item.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
item.description: arXiv:2609.23031v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For two even integers $r_1,r_2$ with $4\leq r_1\leq r_2\leq N/2$, a graph $G$ of even order $N\geq8$ is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=N-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$. We study this property for graphs defined by Cartesian products. Let $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$, where $d\geq2$ and each factor $H_i$ is either $K_2$ or a bipartite graph of even order at least four that has a Hamiltonian cycle and in which every edge lies on a Hamiltonian cycle. We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic if one of the following holds: (i) $d\geq4$; (ii) $d=3$ and at least two factors have order at least four; (iii) $d=3$, exactly one factor has order at least four, and every set of at most two edges of that factor lies on a common Hamiltonian cycle; (iv) $d=2$, both factors have order at least four, and every set of at most two edges of each factor lies on a common Hamiltonian cycle; (v) $G\cong K_2\square K_2\square K_2$. The theorem applies to several families of interconnection networks. In this paper, we give a sharp characterization for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.
item.dc:creator: Ke Lu, Ruichao Niu

item.title: Complete characterization of disconnected one-point unions of cycles with local antimagic chromatic number 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.22808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a graph $G$, characterizing the structural behavior of achieving the minimal local antimagic chromatic number $\chi_{la}(G) = 2$ remains a fundamental open problem in the study of vertex-distinguishing edge labelings. This paper establishes complete characterizations for a significant structural class of disconnected graphs, specifically addressing disconnected one-point unions of cycles with at most three components. By introducing a robust algebraic approach, we show that these specific graph architectures form distinct, manageable solution families under a local antimagic 2-coloring framework. Crucially, our structural framework provides the theoretical basis for extending these complete characterizations to an arbitrary number of components, demonstrating unique edge assignments up to isomorphism. These results offer key insights into the structural properties governing low-chromatic antimagic invariants and offer significant progress toward a unified classification of graphs with $\chi_{la}(G) = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai Chee Shiu

item.title: The degree distribution in bipartite planar maps: applications to the Ising model
item.description: arXiv:math/0211070v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the generating function of bipartite planar maps counted according to the degree distribution of their black and white vertices. This result is applied to the solution of the hard particle and Ising models on random planar lattices. We thus recover and extend some results previously obtained by means of matrix integrals. Proofs are purely combinatorial and rely on the idea that planar maps are conjugacy classes of trees. In particular, these trees explain why the solutions of the Ising and hard particle models on maps of bounded degree are always algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Mireille Bousquet-M\'elou, Gilles Schaeffer

item.title: Ideal transition systems
item.description: arXiv:2412.17320v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study an inductive method of computing initial ideals and Gr\"obner bases for families of ideals in a polynomial ring. This method starts from a given set of pairs $(I,J)$ where $I$ is any ideal and $J$ is a monomial ideal contained in the initial ideal of $I$. These containments become a system of equalities if one can establish a particular transition recurrence among the chosen ideals. We describe explicit constructions of such systems in two motivating cases -- namely, for the ideals of matrix Schubert varieties and their skew-symmetric analogues. Despite many formal similarities with these examples, for the symmetric versions of matrix Schubert varieties, it is an open problem to construct the same kind of transition system. We present several conjectures that would follow from such a construction, while also discussing the special obstructions arising in the symmetric case.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg, Brendan Pawlowski

item.title: Comparing the face rings of a boolean complex and its barycentric subdivision
item.description: arXiv:2507.20037v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the relationship between the Stanley--Reisner ring (a.k.a. face ring) of a simplicial or boolean complex $\Delta$ and that of its barycentric subdivision. These rings share a distinguished parameter subring. S. Murai asked if they are isomorphic, equivariantly with respect to the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)$, as modules over this parameter subring. We show that, in general, the answer is no, but for Cohen--Macaulay complexes in characteristic coprime to $|\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)|$, it is yes, and we give an explicit construction of an isomorphism. To give this construction, we adapt a pair of tools introduced by A. Garsia in 1980. The first one transfers bases from a Stanley--Reisner ring to closely related rings of which it is a Gr\"obner degeneration, and the second identifies bases to transfer.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blum-Smith, Sophie Marques

item.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.18791v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.
item.dc:creator: David Keating, Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Generalizations of tropical Tevelev degrees
item.description: arXiv:2601.21973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study tropical Tevelev degrees arising from maps between certain tropical moduli spaces of curves. Building on work of Dawson and Cavalieri, who defined and computed tropical Tevelev degrees in the case of degree $d = g+1$ and $n = g+3$ marked points, we extend the theory by introducing an additional integer parameter $\ell$. In our framework the curve degree and number of marked points vary as $d = g + 1 + \ell$ and $n = g + 3 + 2\ell$, and we analyze the resulting tropical Tevelev degrees for both positive and negative values of $\ell$. This tropicalizes results of Cela, Pandharipande, and Schmitt on algebraic Tevelev degrees. We then further broaden the framework by introducing generalized tropical Tevelev degrees, providing the tropical counterpart to the generalized Tevelev degrees studied by Cela and Lian. These results establish a wider set of computational and structural patterns for intersection calculations on tropical moduli spaces and reveal new behavior beyond the classical setting.
item.dc:creator: Erin Dawson

item.title: A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.10425v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the kissing number in 19 dimensions is at least 11948, improving the bound of Cohn and Li by 256. Their odd-sign construction reduces the problem to finding a binary code of length 19 and minimum distance 5 inside a 5-punctured extended binary Golay code. In an explicit model $D$ of this ambient code, the 21 words of weights 3 and 4 are exactly the pairwise differences that such a code must avoid. They span a 10-dimensional subcode $K$. We exhibit a 6-dimensional subcode $M\le K$ for which all 21 words lie in only five cosets of $M$. After identifying $K/M$ with $\mathbb F_2^4$, these five cosets are represented by $\Sigma=\{e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4\}$. In the graph on $\mathbb F_2^4$ in which $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $u+v\in\Sigma$, the set $\Sigma$ itself is independent. Lifting its five vertices gives 320 words in $K$, and translating this set through the four cosets of $K$ in $D$ gives a nonlinear code of size 1280 and minimum distance 5.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: Computing distances in braid-move graphs, higher Bruhat orders, and oriented-matroid mutation graphs is NP-hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.03808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A wiring diagram is an arrangement of $m$ pseudolines, every two of which cross exactly once. Reading its crossings from left to right encodes it as a reduced word of the permutation $w_0\in S_m$ that reverses $1,\dots,m$, unique up to commutations, and a braid move $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\leftrightarrow\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$ flips one of its triangles. We prove that deciding whether two wiring diagrams are within a given braid-move distance is NP-complete. Equivalently, deciding flip distance is NP-complete in the higher Bruhat order $B(m,2)$, for triangle flips of marked arrangements of pseudolines, and for rhombic tilings of a $2m$-gon; this answers an open question on flip graphs of pseudoline arrangements (SODA 2024). The reduction is from Vertex Cover: for every graph $G$ we construct two wiring diagrams at braid-move distance $|D|+2\operatorname{VC}(G)$, where $\operatorname{VC}(G)$ is the vertex cover number of $G$ and the Hamming distance $|D|$ is the number of triples of wires whose triangles are oriented differently. The construction glues copies of a seven-wire gadget whose braid-move distance exceeds its Hamming distance by $2$. Adding a line at infinity transfers the construction to rank-$3$ uniform oriented matroids, where two oriented matroids are adjacent in the mutation graph if their chirotopes differ in one basis; so deciding distance in the mutation graph is NP-complete in rank $3$. An iterate of Rambau's expansion of signotopes amplifies the excess and gives NP-hardness in every fixed rank $r\ge4$, and by duality in every fixed corank at least $3$. The same instances show that flip distance in the higher Bruhat orders $B(n,k)$ is NP-complete for every fixed $k\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Tilen Marc

item.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous-Broder Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Aldous-Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but deriving it by summing over the orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered remains difficult. In this paper, we evaluate this sum by establishing an order-mass identity for rooted forests. For real matrices with zero row sums, the identity expresses the sum of order weights associated with each root as a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots, under a nonsingularity condition involving only the sets encountered along the growth orders of the given forest. We prove the identity using linear algebraic tools. With one root, the sum equals one, giving a direct proof of the extended Aldous-Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state. With multiple roots, we derive the forest law produced by the stopped covering walk and show how it differs from the weight-proportional forest law. The identity and the resulting tree and forest laws are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Hugh Zheng
